dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: viśvam etan mahādevi śūnyabhūtaṃ vicintayet | tatraiva ca mano līnaṃ tatas tallayabhājanam ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
dharana.rendering: O great Goddess, let one contemplate this universe as void. The mind dissolves right there, and then one becomes fit for that dissolution.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: concentrate intensely on the idea that the universe is wholly void; the mind is absorbed in it and becomes fit for absorption in the absolute void (Śiva). Singh notes this is the first of several dhāraṇās on the void. Wallis: 'one shares in its dissolution'.
dharana.instruction: Contemplate the whole universe as empty and let the mind rest in that emptiness.

verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 58 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the universe as an open, empty field in which the mind can come to rest.
geometry.svg_hint: a wide empty circle with a faint outline only
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Empty out
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: a crowded picture of the world empties out, and the mind settles into the openness. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Contemplate everything as open and empty
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.secondary: The mind dissolving into that void

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: O great Goddess, let one contemplate this universe as void. The mind dissolves right there, and then one becomes fit for that dissolution.
adiyogi.method_summary: Contemplate everything you know of the world as empty, open, without solidity. Let the mind rest in that openness and dissolve into it. If thoughts come, see them as empty too.

honesty.disclosure: Door 035 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 35 (verse 58) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 035 is dharana 35, verse 58. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. If contemplating emptiness brings low mood or unease, stop and turn to something warm and concrete, such as the breath or a sound. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit or lie down. The map is the universe as an open, empty field.

beats.title: Orientation

beats.title: Breath

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Contemplate everything as empty and open. Let the mind settle into that openness. Thoughts, too, are empty.

beats.title: Reaction cue
